date.as_written: samvat 823 āśvinamāse kṛṣṇapakṣe daśamyāṃ tithāv ādityavāre

notes: The era is not named. I took it as NS because the manuscript is in Newari script and the year is a three-digit "samvat" year (823 + 880 = 1703 CE). "svanimhavantāgṛhanivāsito" is corrupt. It seems to describe where the scribe lived: "dwelling in the house (of) [s]vanimhavantā", perhaps a Newar house or locality name with sva- meaning "his own". This is a residence, not the place of copying. The isolated "2" before "samvat" is unclear; it may be a numbering mark or a verse marker. "śarmmāmūṃ" stands for śarmā amūṃ (= imām). Gaṅgādhara is listed only as author of the commentary. The catalogue's scribe (Devaśaṅkara Śarmā) and date (823) agree with the colophon.
